190	/** Timegrapher panel: trace plus readouts. Reads a Reading; computes nothing but pixels. */
191	import type { Reading } from "../core/timegrapher/analyze";
192	
193	export interface TimegrapherView {
194	  reading: Reading | null;
195	  nominalPeriod: number;
196	  liftAngle: number;
197	  running: boolean;
198	  knocking: boolean;
199	  /** Sim seconds the trace spans, for the honest label. */
200	  spanSeconds: number;
201	  /** Sim seconds per wall second, for the honest label. */
202	  speedup: number;
203	}
204	
205	const fmt = (x: number, d: number) => (Math.abs(x) < 0.5 * 10 ** -d ? "" : x > 0 ? "+" : "−") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(d);
206	
207	export function renderTimegrapher(v: TimegrapherView): string {
208	  const W = 420, H = 300, pad = 36;
209	  const beatMs = (v.nominalPeriod / 2) * 1000;
210	  const yRange = Math.min(20, beatMs / 2); // ±20 ms, wrapping like a real machine's screen
211	  const r = v.reading;
212	  const dots = r
213	    ? r.trace.map((p) => {
214	        const x = pad + ((W - 2 * pad) * p.beat) / Math.max(1, r.trace.length - 1);
215	        let off = ((p.offsetMs + yRange) % (2 * yRange) + 2 * yRange) % (2 * yRange) - yRange; // wrap
216	        const y = H / 2 - (off / yRange) * (H / 2 - pad);
217	        return `<circle class="dot p${p.parity}" cx="${x.toFixed(1)}" cy="${y.toFixed(1)}" r="1.5"/>`;
218	      }).join("")
219	    : "";
220	  const rate = r && v.running ? fmt(r.rateSecondsPerDay, 0) : "—";
221	  const amp = r && v.running ? r.amplitudeDeg.toFixed(0) : "—";
222	  const be = r && v.running ? r.beatErrorMs.toFixed(1) : "—";
223	  // Faint horizontal grid at ±10 ms: half the screen range, purely a reading aid.
224	  const gridY = [H / 2 - (H / 2 - pad) / 2, H / 2 + (H / 2 - pad) / 2];
225	  return `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H + 84}" class="timegrapher" data-rate="${r?.rateSecondsPerDay ?? ""}">
226	  <rect x="0" y="0" width="${W}" height="${H}" rx="2" class="screen"/>
227	  <rect x="0.5" y="0.5" width="${W - 1}" height="${H - 1}" rx="2" class="screen-edge"/>
228	  ${gridY.map((y) => `<line x1="${pad}" y1="${y}" x2="${W - pad}" y2="${y}" class="grid"/>`).join("")}
229	  <line x1="${pad}" y1="${H / 2}" x2="${W - pad}" y2="${H / 2}" class="axis"/>
230	  <text x="${pad}" y="${pad - 10}" class="axislabel">+${yRange.toFixed(0)} ms</text>
231	  <text x="${pad}" y="${H - pad + 18}" class="axislabel">−${yRange.toFixed(0)} ms</text>
232	  <text x="${W - pad}" y="${H - pad + 18}" class="axislabel" text-anchor="end">${v.spanSeconds.toFixed(0)} s of ticks at ${v.speedup}× time</text>
233	  ${v.knocking ? `<text x="${W / 2}" y="${H / 2}" class="warn" text-anchor="middle">Knocking: amplitude unreliable</text>` : ""}
234	  ${v.running ? dots : `<text x="${W / 2}" y="${H / 2}" class="warn" text-anchor="middle">No signal. The watch has stopped.</text>`}
235	  <g class="readouts" transform="translate(0,${H + 10})">
236	    <line x1="${W / 3}" y1="8" x2="${W / 3}" y2="56" class="divider"/>
237	    <line x1="${2 * W / 3}" y1="8" x2="${2 * W / 3}" y2="56" class="divider"/>
238	    <text x="${pad}" y="34" class="big">${rate}<tspan class="unit"> s/day</tspan></text>
239	    <text x="${W / 2}" y="34" class="big" text-anchor="middle">${amp}<tspan class="unit">°</tspan></text>
240	    <text x="${W - pad}" y="34" class="big" text-anchor="end">${be}<tspan class="unit"> ms</tspan></text>
241	    <text x="${pad}" y="56" class="small">rate</text>
242	    <text x="${W / 2}" y="56" class="small" text-anchor="middle">amplitude at ${v.liftAngle}° lift angle</text>
243	    <text x="${W - pad}" y="56" class="small" text-anchor="end">beat error</text>
244	  </g>
245	</svg>`;
246	}

263	const calibre = VINTAGE_18000;
264	const esc = calibre.escapement;
265	const T = nominalPeriod(calibre.beatRate);
266	const TRACE_BEATS = 300;
267	/** Timegrapher clock runs this many times faster than the wall clock (decision: two clocks). */

269	
270	// ---------- state ----------
271	let puzzle: Puzzle | null = PUZZLES[0];
272	let user: WatchSettings = { ...ZERO_SETTINGS };
273	let animSpeed = 1;
274	let animPaused = false;
275	let animTime = T / 4;
276	let simTime = 0;
277	let win: TickWindow = emptyWindow();
278	let pose: EscapementPose = initialPose(esc, 0);
279	let reading: WatchReading = readWatch(calibre.watch, user);
280	let tg: Reading | null = null;
281	let heldSeconds = 0;
282	let solved = false;
283	let answered: number | null = null;
284	let revealHeavySpot = false;
285	/** The control being moved, highlighted on the drawing until `hotUntil` (wall ms). */
286	let hot: Highlight = null;
287	let hotUntil = 0;
288	function touch(part: Highlight) { hot = part; hotUntil = performance.now() + 600; if (animPaused) drawMovement(); }
289	/** On release the glow goes out quickly. */
290	let pointerHeld = false;
291	function release() { pointerHeld = false; if (hot) hotUntil = Math.min(hotUntil, performance.now() + 150); }
292	window.addEventListener("pointerup", release); window.addEventListener("pointercancel", release);
293	let lastWall = performance.now();

295	const spec = (): WatchSpec => (puzzle?.specOverride ? puzzle.specOverride(calibre.watch) : calibre.watch);
296	const effective = (): WatchSettings => {
297	  const f = puzzle?.faults ?? {};

299	    ...user,
300	    regulatorIndex: user.regulatorIndex + (f.regulatorIndex ?? 0),
301	    beatOffsetDeg: user.beatOffsetDeg + (f.beatOffsetDeg ?? 0),
302	    unbalance: user.unbalance + (f.unbalance ?? 0),
303	    heavySpotDeg: f.heavySpotDeg ?? user.heavySpotDeg,
304	    inertiaTrim: user.inertiaTrim,
305	  };
306	};

308	// ---------- DOM ----------
309	const $ = <T extends HTMLElement>(id: string) => document.getElementById(id) as T;
310	const movementEl = $("movement"), tgEl = $("timegrapher"), puzzleEl = $("puzzle");
311	
312	/** Balance angle at an absolute time with the current reading: used only for frozen, named states. */
313	function balanceAngleAt(t: number) {
314	  return reading.running ? reading.amplitudeDeg * Math.sin((2 * Math.PI * t) / reading.period) - reading.beatOffsetDeg : -reading.beatOffsetDeg;
315	}
316	/** Live loop: the oscillator's phase is accumulated frame by frame, so a change of period or
317	 *  amplitude from a slider never jumps the balance (phase from absolute time would). */
318	let balancePhase = Math.PI / 2; // start at +amplitude, fork parked
319	function balanceAngleNow() {
320	  return reading.running ? reading.amplitudeDeg * Math.sin(balancePhase) - reading.beatOffsetDeg : -reading.beatOffsetDeg;
321	}
322	
323	function recompute() {
324	  reading = readWatch(spec(), effective());
325	  if (animPaused) drawMovement();
326	}
327	
328	/** Named verify-render state, if the URL asked for one. */
329	let named: string | null = null;
330	let lastMovementHtml = "";
331	let lastTimegrapherHtml = "";
332	function drawMovement() {
333	  const eff = effective();
334	  const adj = adjustmentShapes(esc, { ...eff, balanceAngle: pose.balanceAngle, amplitudeDeg: reading.amplitudeDeg, revealHeavySpot: revealHeavySpot || (solved && puzzle?.id === "position-error") });
335	  if (hot && !pointerHeld && performance.now() > hotUntil) hot = null;
336	  // Write the DOM only when the picture changed: a stopped watch redraws nothing, so a slider
337	  // being dragged is not fighting sixty SVG replacements a second.
338	  const html = renderMovement(esc, pose, animTime * 1000, adj, hot) + (reading.running ? "" : "<!--stopped-->");
339	  if (html === lastMovementHtml) return;
340	  lastMovementHtml = html;
341	  movementEl.innerHTML = html;
342	  if (named) movementEl.querySelector("svg")!.setAttribute("data-state", named);
343	  if (!reading.running) movementEl.querySelector(".phase")!.textContent = "STOPPED · no torque at the escape wheel";
344	}
345	function drawTimegrapher() {
346	  const html = renderTimegrapher({ reading: tg, nominalPeriod: T, liftAngle: calibre.liftAngle, running: reading.running, knocking: reading.knocking, spanSeconds: (TRACE_BEATS * T) / 2, speedup: SIM_SPEEDUP });
347	  if (html === lastTimegrapherHtml) return;
348	  lastTimegrapherHtml = html;
349	  tgEl.innerHTML = html;
350	}
351	let lastPuzzleHtml = "";
352	/** Re-renders only when the card's content changes: it is called every frame for the hold bar. */
353	function drawPuzzle() {
354	  const html = puzzleHtml();
355	  if (html === lastPuzzleHtml) return;
356	  lastPuzzleHtml = html;
357	  puzzleEl.innerHTML = html;
358	  puzzleEl.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>(".choice").forEach((b) => (b.onclick = () => { answered = Number(b.dataset.choice); if (answered === puzzle!.question!.correct) solved = true; drawPuzzle(); }));
359	}
360	function puzzleHtml(): string {
361	  if (!puzzle) return `<h2>Free play</h2><p>Adjust anything. The timegrapher shows what a watchmaker would see.</p>`;
362	  const idx = PUZZLES.indexOf(puzzle);
363	  return `<h2>Puzzle ${idx + 1} · ${puzzle.title}</h2>
364	    <p class="symptom">${puzzle.symptom}</p>
365	    <p class="goal"><strong>Goal:</strong> ${puzzle.goal}</p>
366	    ${Number.isFinite(puzzle.holdSeconds) ? `<div class="hold"><div class="bar" style="width:${Math.min(100, (100 * heldSeconds) / puzzle.holdSeconds).toFixed(1)}%"></div><span>${solved ? "solved" : `${heldSeconds.toFixed(0)} / ${puzzle.holdSeconds} s in band`}</span></div>` : ""}
367	    ${puzzle.question ? `<div class="question"><p>${puzzle.question.prompt}</p>${puzzle.question.choices.map((c, i) => `<button class="choice ${answered === i ? (i === puzzle!.question!.correct ? "right" : "wrong") : ""}" data-choice="${i}">${c}</button>`).join("")}${answered !== null ? `<p class="verdict">${answered === puzzle.question.correct ? puzzle.question.whyCorrect : "Not quite. Watch the rate as the wind runs down, then try again."}</p>` : ""}</div>` : ""}
368	    ${solved ? `<details open><summary>Why it worked</summary><p>${puzzle.explanation}</p></details>` : ""}`;
369	}
370	function drawControls() {
371	  const show = (name: string) => !puzzle || puzzle.controls.includes(name as never) || puzzle.controls.length === 0;
372	  for (const name of ["regulator", "beat", "wind", "screws", "position"]) $(`ctl-${name}`).hidden = !show(name);
373	  $("ctl-poise").hidden = $("ctl-poise-angle").hidden = !show("poise");
374	  // Controls appear in the order the puzzle lists them; free play keeps the page's own order.
375	  const rank = (name: string) => (puzzle ? puzzle.controls.indexOf(name as never) : -1);
376	  for (const name of ["regulator", "beat", "wind", "screws", "position", "poise"]) {
377	    const order = rank(name) < 0 ? "" : String(rank(name) * 2);
378	    $(`ctl-${name}`).style.order = order;
379	    if (name === "poise") $("ctl-poise-angle").style.order = order === "" ? "" : String(rank(name) * 2 + 1);
380	  }
381	  $("readout-rate").style.order = "99";
382	  $("readout-rate").textContent = reading.running ? `${reading.rateSecondsPerDay >= 0 ? "+" : "−"}${Math.abs(reading.rateSecondsPerDay).toFixed(1)} s/day true rate` : "stopped";
383	}
384	
385	// ---------- frame loop ----------
386	function frame(now: number) {
387	  const wallDt = Math.min(0.1, (now - lastWall) / 1000);
388	  lastWall = now;
389	  if (!animPaused) {
390	    const dt = reading.running ? wallDt * animSpeed : 0; // a stopped watch holds still
391	    animTime += dt;
392	    if (reading.running) balancePhase += (2 * Math.PI * dt) / reading.period;
393	    pose = step(esc, pose, balanceAngleNow(), Math.max(dt, 1e-6), reading.running);
394	    drawMovement();
395	  }
396	  // Timegrapher clock.
397	  const simDt = wallDt * SIM_SPEEDUP;
398	  simTime += simDt;
399	  win = advanceTicks(win, reading, simTime, TRACE_BEATS);
400	  tg = analyze(win.ticks, T, calibre.liftAngle);
401	  drawTimegrapher();
402	  if (puzzle && !solved && Number.isFinite(puzzle.holdSeconds)) {
403	    heldSeconds = puzzle.band(reading, tg) ? heldSeconds + simDt : 0;
404	    if (heldSeconds >= puzzle.holdSeconds) solved = true;
405	    drawPuzzle();
406	  }
407	  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
408	}
409	
410	// ---------- controls ----------
411	function bindRange(id: string, key: keyof WatchSettings, fmt: (v: number) => string, part: Highlight) {
412	  const el = $<HTMLInputElement>(id), out = $(`${id}-value`);

415	  el.onpointerdown = () => { pointerHeld = true; touch(part); };
416	  apply();
417	}

420	bindRange("wind", "hoursSinceWind", (v) => `${v.toFixed(0)} h since wound`, "wind");

430	  amt.onpointerdown = ang.onpointerdown = () => { pointerHeld = true; touch("poise"); };
431	  apply();
432	}

434	$<HTMLSelectElement>("position").innerHTML = POSITIONS.map((p) => `<option value="${p.id}">${p.label}</option>`).join("");

/**
 * Kinematic Swiss lever escapement as a pure stepper. The caller supplies the balance angle
 * each step (from the oscillator model); the fork follows the impulse pin while it is in the
 * notch, and the escape wheel advances as far as the pallet stones physically allow. Phases
 * are read off the contact, never scripted.
 */
import { type EscapementParams, derived } from "./params";
import { distToSegment, len, sub } from "./geom2d";
import { stones, toothPolygons, stonePenetration } from "./shapes";

export type Phase = "lock" | "unlock" | "impulse" | "drop";
export type StoneName = "entry" | "exit";
export type Face = "locking" | "impulse";

export interface EscapementPose {
  balanceAngle: number;
  forkAngle: number;
  wheelAngle: number;
  phase: Phase;
  contact: { stone: StoneName; face: Face } | null;
  /** Count of steps where lever motion drove a stone into a tooth by more than NUDGE_TOL degrees. */
  violations: number;
  /** Largest nudge (degrees) ever needed to clear such a penetration. */
  maxNudge: number;
}

/** Contact solver tolerance: a resting tooth may be pressed this far (scene units) into a face. */
export const CONTACT_TOL = 1e-6;
/** Residual from finite steps along the lock arc. */
const NUDGE_TOL = 1e-3;
/** Largest internal step, seconds. Keeps the contact search well below a tooth width. */
const MAX_SUBSTEP = 1e-4;

/** Fork angle the impulse pin imposes at a given balance angle; the fork parks at a banking
 *  whenever the pin is out of the notch (zero draw: nothing else moves it). */
export function forkFor(p: EscapementParams, balanceAngle: number): number {
  const half = p.liftAngle / 2;
  const x = Math.max(-half, Math.min(half, balanceAngle));
  return (x / half) * derived(p).forkHalf;
}

/** A pose with the wheel settled against whichever stone the given balance angle locks. */
export function initialPose(p: EscapementParams, balanceAngle: number): EscapementPose {
  const fork = forkFor(p, balanceAngle);
  // Settle in small steps so a wheel that starts exactly on a face is recognised as blocked.
  const pitch = derived(p).pitch;
  let wheel = 0, blocked = false;
  for (let i = 0; i < 16 && !blocked; i++) {
    const r = advance(p, fork, wheel, pitch / 8);
    wheel = r.wheel; blocked = r.blocked;
  }
  return { balanceAngle, forkAngle: fork, wheelAngle: wheel, phase: blocked ? "lock" : "drop", contact: blocked ? classify(p, fork, wheel) : null, violations: 0, maxNudge: 0 };
}

/** Advance the escapement by dt seconds while the balance moves from prev.balanceAngle to balanceAngle.
 *  `driven` is whether the gear train still delivers torque to the escape wheel: a run-down watch
 *  has none, so its wheel moves only if a pallet stone pushes it. */
export function step(p: EscapementParams, prev: EscapementPose, balanceAngle: number, dt: number, driven = true): EscapementPose {
  const n = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(dt / MAX_SUBSTEP));
  let pose = prev;
  for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
    const bal = prev.balanceAngle + ((balanceAngle - prev.balanceAngle) * i) / n;
    pose = substep(p, pose, bal, dt / n, driven);
  }
  return pose;
}

function substep(p: EscapementParams, prev: EscapementPose, bal: number, dt: number, driven: boolean): EscapementPose {
  const fork = forkFor(p, bal);
  let wheel = prev.wheelAngle;
  let violations = prev.violations, maxNudge = prev.maxNudge;
  if (worst(p, fork, wheel) > CONTACT_TOL) {
    const nudged = clear(p, fork, wheel);
    const nudge = Math.abs(nudged - wheel);
    if (nudge > maxNudge) maxNudge = nudge;
    if (nudge > NUDGE_TOL) violations++;
    wheel = nudged;
  }
  const r = driven ? advance(p, fork, wheel, p.freeRunSpeed * dt) : { wheel, blocked: worst(p, fork, wheel + 1e-3) > CONTACT_TOL };
  wheel = r.wheel;
  let phase: Phase;
  let contact: EscapementPose["contact"] = null;
  if (!r.blocked) phase = "drop";
  else {
    contact = classify(p, fork, wheel);
    if (contact.face === "impulse") phase = "impulse";
    else {
      const dFork = fork - prev.forkAngle;
      const lifting = (contact.stone === "entry" && dFork < -1e-12) || (contact.stone === "exit" && dFork > 1e-12);
      phase = lifting ? "unlock" : "lock";
    }
  }
  return { balanceAngle: bal, forkAngle: fork, wheelAngle: wheel, phase, contact, violations, maxNudge };
}

/** Largest penetration between any tooth and either stone. */
function worst(p: EscapementParams, forkAngle: number, wheelAngle: number) {
  const { entryStone, exitStone } = stones(p, forkAngle);
  let max = -Infinity;
  for (const tooth of toothPolygons(p, wheelAngle)) {
    for (const s of [entryStone, exitStone]) {
      const pen = stonePenetration(tooth, s);
      if (pen > max) max = pen;
    }
  }
  return max;
}

function classify(p: EscapementParams, forkAngle: number, wheelAngle: number): { stone: StoneName; face: Face } {
  const { entryStone, exitStone } = stones(p, forkAngle);
  let best = { d: Infinity, stone: "entry" as StoneName, face: "locking" as Face };
  for (const tooth of toothPolygons(p, wheelAngle)) {
    const tip = tooth[0];
    for (const [name, s] of [["entry", entryStone], ["exit", exitStone]] as const) {
      const dImp = distToSegment(tip, s.corner, s.letoff);
      const dLock = Math.abs(len(sub(tip, s.pivot)) - s.lockRadius);
      if (dImp < best.d) best = { d: dImp, stone: name, face: "impulse" };
      if (dLock < best.d) best = { d: dLock, stone: name, face: "locking" };
    }
  }
  return { stone: best.stone, face: best.face };
}

/** Nearest wheel angle (either direction, within half a degree) at which the pose no longer penetrates. */
function clear(p: EscapementParams, fork: number, wheel: number) {
  const search = (dir: 1 | -1) => {
    let lo = wheel, hi = wheel + dir * 0.5;
    if (worst(p, fork, hi) > CONTACT_TOL) return Infinity;
    for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
      const mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
      if (worst(p, fork, mid) <= CONTACT_TOL) hi = mid; else lo = mid;
    }
    return hi;
  };
  const fwd = search(1), back = search(-1);
  if (fwd === Infinity && back === Infinity) return wheel + 0.5; // hopeless; let the violation show
  return Math.abs(fwd - wheel) <= Math.abs(back - wheel) ? fwd : back;
}

/** Move the wheel forward by up to `maxStep` degrees, stopping at first contact. */
function advance(p: EscapementParams, fork: number, wheel: number, maxStep: number) {
  const target = wheel + maxStep;
  if (worst(p, fork, target) <= CONTACT_TOL) return { wheel: target, blocked: false };
  let lo = wheel, hi = target;
  for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
    const mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
    if (worst(p, fork, mid) <= CONTACT_TOL) lo = mid; else hi = mid;
  }
  return { wheel: lo, blocked: true };
}
/**
 * Geometry of the adjustments a watchmaker touches, derived from the settings so every slider
 * moves something on the drawing. Pure: parameters and settings in, points out. The renderer
 * draws these and computes nothing. Nothing here feeds the physics; the physics reads the same
 * settings directly (src/core/watch.ts).
 */
import { type EscapementParams, rad } from "./params";
import { type Vec, add, polar, v } from "./geom2d";
import { fixedPoints } from "./shapes";
import type { Position } from "../watch";

export interface AdjustmentInput {
  balanceAngle: number;
  /** Regulator index angle, degrees; positive toward Fast. Drawn 1:1. */
  regulatorIndex: number;
  /** Stud carrier rotation, degrees. Drawn 1:1. */
  beatOffsetDeg: number;
  /** Fractional inertia change from the timing screws. */
  inertiaTrim: number;
  position: Position;
  /** Where weight is being removed on the rim, and how much (kg·m). */
  poiseCorrection: number;
  poiseCorrectionDeg: number;
  /** The hidden heavy spot, shown only once revealed. */
  heavySpotDeg: number;
  unbalance: number;
  revealHeavySpot: boolean;
  /** Current swing amplitude, degrees, for the swing arc. */
  amplitudeDeg: number;
}

export interface AdjustmentShapes {
  /** Hairspring as a polyline from the collet (inner end, turns with the balance) to the stud (fixed). */
  hairspring: Vec[];
  /** Outer attachment of the hairspring; moves with the beat adjustment. */
  stud: Vec;
  /** The arc the stud carrier can swing through, for drawing the carrier's slot. */
  studTrack: { centre: Vec; radius: number; fromDeg: number; toDeg: number };
  /** Regulator: pivoted on the balance axis, its pins straddle the outer coil at `pins`. */
  regulator: { arm: [Vec, Vec]; pins: [Vec, Vec]; scale: { fast: Vec; slow: Vec; centre: Vec }; indexDeg: number };
  /** Timing screws on the rim: head position and how far it stands proud (positive = out = slower). */
  screws: { head: Vec; proud: number; angleDeg: number }[];
  /** Weight removed for poising: a cut in the rim at the chosen angle, depth ∝ amount. */
  poiseCut: { at: Vec; depth: number; angleDeg: number } | null;
  /** The hidden heavy spot, if revealed. */
  heavySpot: { at: Vec; angleDeg: number } | null;
  /** The balance's swing: the impulse pin's arc from −amplitude to +amplitude about the notch centre. */
  swingArc: { centre: Vec; radius: number; fromDeg: number; toDeg: number };
  /** Rotation to apply to the whole movement so "crown down" points down the page, and where gravity points. */
  view: { rotationDeg: number; gravity: "into-page" | "out-of-page" | "down" };
}

/** Rim angle of the crown relative to the movement's +x axis: crown at 3 o'clock. */
const CROWN_AT_DEG = 0;

const VIEW: Record<Position, AdjustmentShapes["view"]> = {
  DU: { rotationDeg: 0, gravity: "into-page" },
  DD: { rotationDeg: 0, gravity: "out-of-page" },
  CU: { rotationDeg: 90 - CROWN_AT_DEG, gravity: "down" },
  CR: { rotationDeg: 0 - CROWN_AT_DEG, gravity: "down" },
  CD: { rotationDeg: -90 - CROWN_AT_DEG, gravity: "down" },
  CL: { rotationDeg: 180 - CROWN_AT_DEG, gravity: "down" },
};

export const HAIRSPRING_TURNS = 5;
/** Regulator and stud sit on the balance cock at this angle from +x at zero adjustment (top of the drawing). */
export const COCK_ANGLE_DEG = 90;
/** Inertia trim of ±0.4 % draws as ±4 units of screw travel. */
export const SCREW_PROUD_PER_TRIM = 1000;
/** A poise cut of 10 µg·cm draws 4 units deep. */
export const POISE_CUT_PER_UNBALANCE = 4 / 10e-11;

export function adjustmentShapes(p: EscapementParams, a: AdjustmentInput): AdjustmentShapes {
  const { balanceCentre: B } = fixedPoints(p);
  const R = p.balanceRadius;
  const rInner = 0.12 * R, rOuter = 0.72 * R;

  // Hairspring: an Archimedean spiral whose inner end is pinned to the balance (angle follows the
  // balance 1:1) and whose outer end is pinned to the stud. Between them the coil angle is
  // interpolated, so winding the balance tightens or opens the coils visibly.
  const studAngle = COCK_ANGLE_DEG + a.beatOffsetDeg;
  const innerAngle = COCK_ANGLE_DEG - a.balanceAngle; // balance turns the same sense as the impulse pin
  const sweep = 360 * HAIRSPRING_TURNS + (studAngle - innerAngle);
  const N = 160;
  const hairspring: Vec[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i <= N; i++) {
    const s = i / N;
    hairspring.push(add(B, polar(rInner + (rOuter - rInner) * s, rad(innerAngle + sweep * s))));
  }
  const stud = add(B, polar(rOuter, rad(studAngle)));
  const studTrack = { centre: B, radius: rOuter, fromDeg: COCK_ANGLE_DEG - 12, toDeg: COCK_ANGLE_DEG + 12 };

  // Regulator: index lever pivoted on the balance axis; toward Fast (positive) the pins move
  // toward the stud, shortening the active coil. Drawn 1:1 with the model's index angle.
  const indexDeg = COCK_ANGLE_DEG + 24 - a.regulatorIndex; // pins rest 24° from the stud; Fast closes the gap
  const pinsAt = add(B, polar(rOuter, rad(indexDeg)));
  const across = polar(2.2, rad(indexDeg));
  const regulator = {
    arm: [B, add(B, polar(R * 1.15, rad(indexDeg)))] as [Vec, Vec],
    pins: [add(pinsAt, across), add(pinsAt, scaleNeg(across))] as [Vec, Vec],
    scale: {
      fast: add(B, polar(R * 1.25, rad(COCK_ANGLE_DEG + 24 - 4))),
      slow: add(B, polar(R * 1.25, rad(COCK_ANGLE_DEG + 24 + 4))),
      centre: add(B, polar(R * 1.25, rad(COCK_ANGLE_DEG + 24))),
    },
    indexDeg,
  };

  // Timing screws: four pairs on the rim, turning with the balance; proud = out = more inertia.
  const proud = a.inertiaTrim * SCREW_PROUD_PER_TRIM;
  const screws = [0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270, 315].map((deg) => {
    const angleDeg = deg - a.balanceAngle;
    return { head: add(B, polar(R + proud, rad(angleDeg))), proud, angleDeg };
  });

  const poiseCut = a.poiseCorrection > 0
    ? { at: add(B, polar(R, rad(a.poiseCorrectionDeg - a.balanceAngle))), depth: a.poiseCorrection * POISE_CUT_PER_UNBALANCE, angleDeg: a.poiseCorrectionDeg - a.balanceAngle }
    : null;
  const heavySpot = a.revealHeavySpot && a.unbalance > 0
    ? { at: add(B, polar(R, rad(a.heavySpotDeg - a.balanceAngle))), angleDeg: a.heavySpotDeg - a.balanceAngle }
    : null;

  const { pinOrbit } = fixedPoints(p);
  const swingArc = { centre: B, radius: pinOrbit, fromDeg: -90 - a.amplitudeDeg, toDeg: -90 + a.amplitudeDeg };
  return { hairspring, stud, studTrack, regulator, screws, poiseCut, heavySpot, swingArc, view: VIEW[a.position] };
}

const scaleNeg = (q: Vec): Vec => v(-q.x, -q.y);
/**
 * The instrument. Reads a window of ticks and reports what a bench timegrapher reports.
 * Formulas per docs/research/02-beat-rates-and-timegrapher.md (verified against the `tg`
 * open-source timegrapher):
 *   rate  = (T_nominal / T_measured − 1) · 86400          (+ = fast)
 *   beat error = |d2 − d1| / 2                             (equals trace-line separation)
 *   amplitude = (lift / 2) / sin(π · dt / T)               (dt = unlock-to-lock time)
 */
import type { Tick } from "../oscillator/ticks";

export interface Reading {
  rateSecondsPerDay: number;
  beatErrorMs: number;
  amplitudeDeg: number;
  /** One point per tick: beat index and the tick's offset from the nominal grid, ms. */
  trace: { beat: number; offsetMs: number; parity: 0 | 1 }[];
  beats: number;
}

export function analyze(ticks: Tick[], nominalPeriod: number, liftAngleDeg: number): Reading | null {
  if (ticks.length < 4) return null;
  const beat = nominalPeriod / 2;
  const n = ticks.length;
  // Measured period from first and last tick of matching parity (whole periods between them).
  const lastSame = n - 1 - ((n - 1) % 2);
  const periods = lastSame / 2;
  const measuredPeriod = (ticks[lastSame].t - ticks[0].t) / periods;
  const rateSecondsPerDay = (nominalPeriod / measuredPeriod - 1) * 86400;

  let d1 = 0, d2 = 0, c1 = 0, c2 = 0;
  for (let i = 1; i < n; i++) {
    const d = ticks[i].t - ticks[i - 1].t;
    if (ticks[i - 1].parity === 0) { d1 += d; c1++; } else { d2 += d; c2++; }
  }
  const beatErrorMs = c1 && c2 ? (Math.abs(d2 / c2 - d1 / c1) / 2) * 1000 : 0;

  const dt = ticks.reduce((a, k) => a + k.liftDuration, 0) / n;
  const amplitudeDeg = liftAngleDeg / 2 / Math.sin((Math.PI * dt) / measuredPeriod);

  const trace = ticks.map((k, i) => ({ beat: i, offsetMs: (k.t - ticks[0].t - i * beat) * 1000, parity: k.parity }));
  return { rateSecondsPerDay, beatErrorMs, amplitudeDeg, trace, beats: n };
}
/**
 * Tick times of a sinusoidal balance, θ(t) = A·sin(ωt), that engages the fork whenever it
 * crosses the notch centre. If the hairspring's rest position is offset from the notch centre
 * by `beatOffset`, the crossings are unevenly spaced: that is beat error, and it grows as
 * amplitude falls (the same offset is a larger fraction of a smaller swing).
 *
 * Each tick also carries the unlock-to-lock time the timegrapher hears: the time the balance
 * spends inside the lift angle, which is what encodes amplitude in the sound.
 * See docs/research/02-beat-rates-and-timegrapher.md.
 */
export interface Tick {
  /** Absolute time of the tick (balance passing the notch centre), seconds. */
  t: number;
  /** Time from the unlock pulse to the lock pulse within this beat, seconds. */
  liftDuration: number;
  /** Alternates each beat. */
  parity: 0 | 1;
}

export interface TickSource {
  /** Actual period of the balance, seconds. */
  period: number;
  /** Amplitude, degrees. */
  amplitude: number;
  /** Notch centre's angle from the hairspring rest position, degrees. Zero = in beat. */
  beatOffset: number;
  /** Balance travel while engaged with the fork, degrees. */
  liftAngle: number;
}

/** Time the balance spends crossing an angular band of `band` degrees centred on `centre`. */
function crossingDuration(s: TickSource, centre: number, band: number): number {
  const omega = (2 * Math.PI) / s.period;
  const A = s.amplitude;
  const lo = Math.max(-A, Math.min(A, centre - band / 2));
  const hi = Math.max(-A, Math.min(A, centre + band / 2));
  return Math.abs(Math.asin(hi / A) - Math.asin(lo / A)) / omega;
}

/** The two half-period intervals between successive crossings of the notch centre. */
export function beatIntervals(s: TickSource): [number, number] {
  if (Math.abs(s.beatOffset) >= s.amplitude) return [s.period, 0]; // never crosses: stopped
  const omega = (2 * Math.PI) / s.period;
  const phi = Math.asin(s.beatOffset / s.amplitude);
  const d1 = (Math.PI - 2 * phi) / omega;
  return [d1, s.period - d1];
}

/** `count` consecutive ticks starting at time `start` (which is itself a tick of parity 0). */
export function tickTimes(s: TickSource, start: number, count: number): Tick[] {
  const [d1, d2] = beatIntervals(s);
  const lift = crossingDuration(s, s.beatOffset, s.liftAngle);
  const out: Tick[] = [];
  let t = start;
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    out.push({ t, liftDuration: lift, parity: (i % 2) as 0 | 1 });
    t += i % 2 === 0 ? d1 : d2;
  }
  return out;
}

/** Movement speed control: a stepped slider inside the drawing panel.
 *  It drives the hidden <select id="speed"> that main.ts listens to, so the frame loop is untouched. */

export const SPEED_STOPS: { value: number; label: string }[] = [
  { value: 0.01, label: "1/100" },
  { value: 0.05, label: "1/20" },
  { value: 0.1, label: "1/10" },
  { value: 0.2, label: "1/5" },
  { value: 1, label: "real time" },
];
export const DEFAULT_SPEED = 0.1;

export function mountSpeedControl(host: HTMLElement, select: HTMLSelectElement, pause: HTMLElement): void {
  const start = Math.max(0, SPEED_STOPS.findIndex((s) => s.value === DEFAULT_SPEED));
  host.innerHTML = `<label class="tempo-label" for="speed-slider">Movement speed</label>
    <div class="tempo-track">
      <input id="speed-slider" type="range" min="0" max="${SPEED_STOPS.length - 1}" step="1" value="${start}" aria-valuetext="${SPEED_STOPS[start].label}" />
      <div class="tempo-stops" aria-hidden="true" style="--n:${SPEED_STOPS.length - 1}">${SPEED_STOPS.map((s, i) => `<span style="--i:${i}">${s.label}</span>`).join("")}</div>
    </div>`;
  host.appendChild(pause);
  const slider = host.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("#speed-slider")!;
  const apply = () => {
    const stop = SPEED_STOPS[Number(slider.value)];
    slider.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", stop.label);
    host.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(".tempo-stops span").forEach((el, i) => el.classList.toggle("on", i === Number(slider.value)));
    select.value = String(stop.value);
    select.dispatchEvent(new Event("change"));
  };
  slider.oninput = apply;
  apply();
}

## Signal Guide

- `brightness`: warm / balanced / bright, based on spectral centroid and high-frequency energy.
- `highFrequencyRisk`: low / medium / high. High-risk SFX can feel sharp, hissy, clicky, or fatiguing if repeated.
- `brightBurden`: high-frequency energy weighted by level and duration. This separates sustained glassy ringing from short clicks.
- `highActiveDuration`: how long bright energy stays active above a useful level.
- `envelopeShape`: transient / textured / continuous. Continuous bright sounds are more fatiguing than sparse textured sounds.
- `transient.sharpness`: higher values feel clickier or more percussive.
- `duration`: short sounds work for UI and typing; longer sounds work for reveals and transitions.

# HyperFrames Composition Project

This folder is a [HyperFrames](https://hyperframes.heygen.com) video: HTML, CSS and seekable
animations (GSAP by default) that the `hyperframes` CLI previews in the browser and renders to
MP4.

## Skills — read these first

**Invoke the relevant skill before writing or modifying compositions.** Skills encode framework-specific patterns (e.g., `window.__timelines` registration, `data-*` attribute semantics, shader-compatible CSS rules) that generic web docs don't cover, so compositions written without them break.

**Doing anything with HyperFrames?** Start at `/hyperframes`. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (each kind of film, story, motion, look, sound, review, captions, overlays). Read it first, especially when there's no project context to orient you.

- `/hyperframes` — read first for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays. Holds the render contract and the work loop.
- `/hyperframes-cli` — the CLI by job: scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render, publish, project history.
- `/hyperframes-registry` — ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source. Search it before hand-building any named visual.
- `/media-use` — get or make any media (music, sound effects, images, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades) and mix placed audio.
- `/reverse-any-video` — rebuild any video file as an editable HyperFrames project and check it against the original frame by frame (HyperFrames Pro).
- `/style-sampling` — make a new episode on your topic in one of five proven styles (HyperFrames Pro).
- `/figma` — bring a Figma design, frame, logo or brand into a video.
- `/slideshow` — a presentation or pitch deck. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4.
- `/remotion-to-hyperframes` — bring existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, or renders from other tools) and verify it frame by frame against the original.

**Changing how real footage or images look or reveal?** Load `/media-use` and read its `references/media-treatments.md` before editing, even when the request only says dark, flat, boring, retro, private, or “make the reveal cooler.” It governs how footage is treated, never whether media may be used. Use canonical media treatments and seek-safe motion; do not improvise equivalent CSS/SVG filters or overlays.

> **Tailwind v4 projects** (`hyperframes init --tailwind`): see `hyperframes-cli/references/init-and-scaffold.md` (Tailwind).

> **Using a HyperFrames plugin?** Load skills from that installed bundle and follow
> its `hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md` execution rules. The person updates
> the plugin through its plugin manager; the standalone commands below do not apply.
>
> **Standalone skill missing or stale?** Installing and updating skills is the person's step:
> tell them which skill is missing or stale, and do not run the install yourself. For the user:
> `npx hyperframes skills update <name>` installs/refreshes that skill, and bare
> `npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes the core set plus everything already installed —
> neither pulls the full set. Newly installed skills load in a new agent session.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev          # human-operated foreground preview (blocks until stopped)
npx hyperframes preview --background  # agent-safe persistent Studio preview
npx hyperframes preview --status      # verify the persistent preview is listening
npx hyperframes preview --stop        # stop it when review is finished
npm run check        # lint + runtime + layout + motion + contrast (one command)
npx hyperframes snapshot --at 1,3,5  # PNG frames at those seconds, to look at before rendering
npm run render       # render to MP4
npm run publish      # publish and get a shareable link
npx hyperframes lint --verbose  # include info-level findings
npx hyperframes lint --json     # machine-readable output for CI
npx hyperframes docs <topic> # reference docs in terminal
```

> **Agents must use `npx hyperframes preview --background` for Studio handoff.** Do not rely
> on a shell/tool `run_in_background` wrapper around `npm run dev`: that foreground process
> remains owned by the invoking session and can disappear while the browser stays open,
> leaving refreshes at `ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT`. Verify with `preview --status`. The desktop
> app can't edit the project while this preview runs, so `npx hyperframes open` stops it first.
> If you hand the project to the app another way, run `preview --stop` before you do. Otherwise keep it
> alive through review, and stop it explicitly with `preview --stop` afterward.

> **Back from the desktop app.** Once this project was opened in the HyperFrames desktop app, run `npx hyperframes catch-up` before your next change here: it lists what the person asked Framey in the app and which files changed since.

> **Pinned CLI version.** These scripts pin an exact `hyperframes@X.Y.Z` so this project re-renders identically over time. Weeks later that pin lags fixes shipped since. To move up: `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project . --check` (shows the delta), then `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project .` to rewrite the pins. Always unpinned — the pinned script re-runs the old version against itself.

## Documentation

**For quick reference**, use the local CLI docs command (no network required):

```bash
npx hyperframes docs <topic>
```

Topics: `data-attributes`, `gsap`, `compositions`, `rendering`, `examples`, `troubleshooting`

**For full documentation**, discover pages via the machine-readable index — do NOT guess URLs:

```
https://hyperframes.heygen.com/llms.txt
```

## Project Structure

- `index.html` — main composition (root timeline)
- `compositions/` — sub-compositions referenced via `data-composition-src`
- `meta.json` — project metadata (id, name)
- `transcript.json` — whisper word-level transcript (if generated)

## Linting — ALWAYS RUN AFTER CHANGES

After creating or editing any `.html` composition, **always** run the full check before considering the task complete:

```bash
npm run check
```

Fix all errors before presenting the result. Warnings should be reviewed before rendering.

Then look at what you changed: `npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>` (or `--range START,END`, `--composition <id>`) at the moments you edited, and read the frames before you reply. A passing check does not show how it looks.

## Key Rules

1. Every timed element needs `data-start` and a duration. `data-start` is what marks it as timed; `data-track-index` is an optional Studio display lane the render never reads
2. Give timed visual elements `class="clip"`. The framework keys visibility off `data-start`, not the class, but the shared `.clip` CSS is what gives a scene its full-frame box, and `lint` warns without it
3. Register one paused root timeline per composition on `window.__timelines`:
   ```js
   window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
   window.__timelines["composition-id"] = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
   ```
   Scene timelines manually added to this root must not be paused. A paused
   child does not advance when the root is seeked. The runtime activates
   registered composition siblings, not arbitrary nested scene timelines.
4. A video with sound keeps it on the `<video>` (`data-has-audio="true"`, no `muted`). Use a separate `<audio>` for music, voiceover, replacement audio, J/L cuts, or audio detached in Studio. Silent footage and b-roll: `muted`.
5. Sub-compositions use `data-composition-src="compositions/file.html"` to reference other HTML files
6. Only deterministic logic — no `Date.now()`, no `Math.random()`, no network fetches

# Brag Plan: The Watchmaker's Bench

## What is this app?
A browser bench where you learn why a mechanical watch runs fast or slow by diagnosing and regulating a live, simulated movement, read through a timegrapher (rate in s/day, amplitude in degrees, beat error in ms).

## The angle
A watch comes in with a complaint. The video is the repair: the timegrapher shows the fault as a sloping phosphor line, one slider on the bench moves a real part on the drawing, and the line goes flat. Nothing in the video is a mock-up: the movement drawing and the timegrapher are rendered frame by frame by the app's own sim core and SVG renderers (`src/core`, `src/view`), so every number on screen is the number the app would show.

## Hook (first 2-3 seconds)
Dark instrument screen. A phosphor trace draws itself, sloping away from the centre line, over the sound of a ticking watch. The readout settles on **+41 s/day**. One line, verbatim from puzzle 1: *"The owner says it gains about 40 seconds a day."*

## Key moments (the middle)
- The movement on the drafting sheet: escape wheel, lever and balance ticking in slow motion, the phase caption changing (Lock, Unlock, Impulse, Drop), three drafting labels landing one by one.
- Puzzle 1 solved live: cursor drags **Regulator index** toward S, the regulator glows ruby on the drawing, the rate falls from +41 to 0, the trace flattens, the hold bar fills to "solved", "Why it worked" opens.
- Three more jobs: "Out of beat" (two trace lines merge into one), "Afternoon slump" (the trace bends as the wind runs down), "Position error" (the slope flips between crown up and crown down). Each mini trace is the real sim running that puzzle.

## Outro / punchline
"The Watchmaker's Bench" / "Why a watch keeps bad time, and how you fix it." / watchmakers-bench.pages.dev, with the balance still swinging.

## User flow worth showing
Read the symptom and the sloping trace → drag Regulator index toward S (the part lights up on the drawing) → rate reads 0 s/day, hold bar fills, "solved", explanation.

## Tone
- Preset: polished
- Creative direction: quiet drafting-sheet product film; an instrument, a drawing, one adjustment
- Interpretation: few scenes, long holds, no hype copy. Motion comes from the watch itself (the balance swing, the trace) rather than from decoration. Ruby is the only accent, as in the app.

## Format: landscape — 1920x1080
## Duration: 24.5 seconds

## Visual identity (from the project)
- Background: `#dfe3d9` (desk mat) with the sheet `#f6f7f2` / paper `#fbfcf8`
- Accent: `#b2322b` (ruby)
- Text: `#1c2733` (blue-black ink); on the instrument `#eef1ea` on case `#202528`, screen `#10261f`, phosphor `#9be39b` / `#e0e39b`
- Display font: Avenir Next (the app's own stack: "Avenir Next", "Segoe UI", "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif)
- Body font: same
- Strongest visual element: the phosphor timegrapher trace against the ink-on-paper movement drawing

## Share copy (draft)
A watch that gains 40 seconds a day, and the one slider that fixes it. The Watchmaker's Bench: diagnose a live, simulated movement and regulate it, reading the timegrapher the way a watchmaker does.

## Audio direction
- Role: warm bed with sparse professional accents
- Music: `happy-beats-business-moves-vol-12-by-ende-dot-app.mp3` (steady and clean), trimmed to the film length
- Music treatment: starts at 0 under the ticking, bed volume about 0.3, fades out over the last 1.5 s
- Music cue guidance: bundled preset read (`cues/happy-beats-business-moves-vol-12-by-ende-dot-app.music-cues.md`, 109.96 BPM). Strong-cue locks: 8.74 s (cursor grabs the regulator), 13.11 s ("solved"), 22.93 s (URL lands). Beat grid: movement ticks land on every beat in scene 2 (0.545 s apart, non-text accents); drafting labels on 5.34 / 6.56 / 7.64 (every other beat, they are text); job cards on 16.93 / 18.02 / 19.10 (every other beat).
- Audio-reactive treatment: subtle; music RMS breathes the phosphor glow around the instrument screen. No waveform or equalizer visuals.
- SFX posture: sparse, motion-matched: a watch-tick bed under the hook, one click on the grab, one soft bell on "solved", soft drops for the three job cards, one bong on the URL.
- Audio-coupled moments: ticking under the growing trace; click on slider grab; bell on solved; card drops.
- Restraint rule: no whooshes, no risers, nothing louder than the bed except the bell.

## Storyboard

### Scene 1 — The complaint — 0.00 to 3.82 (3.82 s)
Dark case colour full frame. The real timegrapher (puzzle 1 as loaded) large on the right; its trace grows from the left, sloping; readout climbs to +41 s/day, 280°, 0.0 ms. Left: "The owner says it gains about 40 seconds a day." (9 words, settled about 2.9 s).
Sequential/interaction: the trace draws itself tick by tick.

Audio-coupled idea: tick bed at 5 ticks a second (18,000 bph) for the length of the scene.
Music: bed enters quietly from 0.

Paper drafting sheet with the 32 px grid. The real movement drawing as hero on the right, running, phase caption live. Left: "The Watchmaker's Bench" then "Diagnose a live movement and regulate it." (trimmed from the app's tagline). Three drafting labels with leader lines: "escape wheel", "lever", "balance".
Sequential/interaction: labels arrive one by one (5.34, 6.56, 7.64), each held to the end of the scene.

The bench itself, three columns as in the app: job card (Puzzle 1 · Runs fast, symptom, goal, hold bar), movement, timegrapher with Regulator index and State of wind under it. Cursor grabs the regulator thumb (8.74), drags toward S until 10.4; the regulator index glows ruby on the drawing; the value reads "−1.20° (toward S)"; the rate falls and the trace flattens; hold bar fills; at 13.11 "solved" and "Why it worked" opens with its first sentence marked: "The regulator index had been pushed toward F."
Sequential/interaction: simulated drag on the real slider; counter and hold bar driven by the sim. The instrument clock is sped up in the edit so the 60-second hold fits; the label on the screen still reads what the app shows.
Audio intent: focus, then release.
Audio-coupled idea: click on grab; soft bell on solved.
Transition mood: clean → Scene 4

### Scene 4 — Three more jobs — 16.38 to 20.75 (4.37 s)
Paper. Header "Three more jobs on the bench". Three job cards arrive one by one (16.93, 18.02, 19.10): "Puzzle 2 · Out of beat", "Puzzle 3 · Afternoon slump", "Puzzle 4 · Position error". Each card carries a small live timegrapher running that puzzle: lines merge as the beat adjustment moves; the trace bends as hours since wind go 0 → 30; the slope flips from crown up to crown down.
Sequential/interaction: cards one by one, every other beat; all three held together to the end.
Audio intent: light, even.
Audio-coupled idea: one soft drop per card.
Transition mood: soft → Scene 5

### Scene 5 — Outro — 20.75 to 24.50 (3.75 s)
Paper. "The Watchmaker's Bench" large; "Why a watch keeps bad time, and how you fix it."; URL "watchmakers-bench.pages.dev" lands at 22.93. The movement runs small at the right. Music credit in small type.
Sequential/interaction: none.
Audio intent: resolve; bed fades.
Audio-coupled idea: one bong on the URL.
Transition mood: fade out.

**Music mood for this video:** steady, clean, restrained
**Audio summary:** a ticking watch under a quiet bed, one click when the hand touches the regulator, a soft bell when the watch comes right, and a fade.

## Grounding notes
- Every on-screen number comes from the app's sim (`readWatch`, `advanceTicks`, `analyze`) and both drawings from `renderMovement` / `renderTimegrapher`.
- Copy sources: puzzle titles, symptom, goal, explanation from `src/puzzles/index.ts`; title and tagline from `index.html`; "why it keeps bad time and how you fix it" from `CLAUDE.md`; labels from `GLOSSARY.md` terms; URL from `README.md`.
- UI copy says "lever", never "Swiss lever" (project decision).

/**
 * Pure geometry: parameters + state in, shapes out. The renderer draws these; the
 * simulation uses the same description for contact, so what you see is what is computed.
 * Coordinates are y-up with the escape wheel centred on the origin. Wheel angle is
 * degrees of CLOCKWISE rotation (teeth travel from the entry stone to the exit stone).
 */
import { type EscapementParams, derived, rad } from "./params";
import { type Polygon, type Vec, add, scale, polar, rotateAbout, sub, len, dot, v } from "./geom2d";

export interface Pose { balanceAngle: number; forkAngle: number; wheelAngle: number }
// (Pose is the subset of EscapementPose the drawing needs.)

/**
 * A pallet stone, exactly: an annular sector about the fork pivot, cut by the impulse
 * plane. The locking face is the arc at radius `lockRadius`, so lever rotation slides it
 * along itself (zero draw). Angles are radians about the pivot, measured with atan2.
 */
export interface Stone {
  pivot: Vec;
  lockRadius: number;
  /** Radial band about the pivot that holds the stone body; one bound is the lock arc. */
  rLo: number;
  rHi: number;
  /** Impulse plane: inside the stone when dot(q - corner, normal) >= 0. */
  corner: Vec;
  normal: Vec;
  /** Back edge, from the let-off corner away from the wheel: inside when dot(q - letoff, backNormal) >= 0. */
  letoff: Vec;
  backNormal: Vec;
  /** Top edge, closing the slab: inside when dot(q - outerEnd, topNormal) >= 0. */
  outerEnd: Vec;
  backEnd: Vec;
  topNormal: Vec;
  /** Whether the stone body lies at radii below (`inside`) or above the lock arc. */
  bodyInside: boolean;
}

/** Signed depth of a point inside a stone: positive inside, negative outside. */
export function stoneDepth(q: Vec, s: Stone): number {
  const r = len(sub(q, s.pivot));
  return Math.min(
    r - s.rLo,
    s.rHi - r,
    dot(sub(q, s.corner), s.normal),
    dot(sub(q, s.letoff), s.backNormal),
    dot(sub(q, s.outerEnd), s.topNormal),
  );
}

/** Largest depth of any tooth vertex inside a stone. */
export function stonePenetration(tooth: Polygon, stone: Stone): number {
  let max = -Infinity;
  for (const q of tooth) {
    const dd = stoneDepth(q, stone);
    if (dd > max) max = dd;
  }
  return max;
}

/** Outline for drawing: the lock arc chorded finely, then the three straight edges. */
export function stoneOutline(s: Stone, chords = 24): Polygon {
  const a0 = Math.atan2(s.corner.y - s.pivot.y, s.corner.x - s.pivot.x);
  let a1 = Math.atan2(s.outerEnd.y - s.pivot.y, s.outerEnd.x - s.pivot.x);
  while (a1 - a0 > Math.PI) a1 -= 2 * Math.PI;
  while (a1 - a0 < -Math.PI) a1 += 2 * Math.PI;
  const arc = Array.from({ length: chords + 1 }, (_, i) => add(s.pivot, polar(s.lockRadius, a0 + ((a1 - a0) * i) / chords)));
  return [...arc, s.backEnd, s.letoff];
}

export function fixedPoints(p: EscapementParams) {
  const d = derived(p);
  const forkPivot = v(0, d.pivotDistance);
  const pinOrbit = (p.forkLength * rad(d.forkHalf)) / rad(p.liftAngle / 2);
  const balanceCentre = v(0, d.pivotDistance + p.forkLength + pinOrbit);
  return { d, forkPivot, balanceCentre, pinOrbit };

/** Escapement geometry. Every shape and motion derives from these numbers; nothing is hand-drawn.
 *  Part of a calibre's definition in the catalog. */
export interface EscapementParams {
  /** Escape wheel tooth count. */
  teeth: number;
  /** Escape wheel tip radius, scene units. */
  wheelRadius: number;
  /** Balance travel (degrees) during which the impulse pin is in the fork notch. */
  liftAngle: number;
  /** Lever rotation (degrees) spent unlocking before the tooth tip reaches the pallet corner. */
  lockAngle: number;
  /** Lever rotation (degrees) during which the tooth tip slides on the impulse face. */
  liftLever: number;
  /** Lever rotation (degrees) after drop before the lever reaches its banking. */
  runToBanking: number;
  /** Escape wheel rotation (degrees) in free flight between leaving one pallet and landing on the other. */
  drop: number;
  /** Escape wheel speed in free flight, degrees per second. Must exceed the fastest rate at
   *  which an impulse face can recede, or the stepper reports a false drop mid-impulse. */
  freeRunSpeed: number;
  /** Fork length from its pivot to the notch, scene units. Drives rendering only. */
  forkLength: number;
  /** Balance wheel radius, scene units. Drives rendering only. */
  balanceRadius: number;
}

/** Quantities the geometry needs, derived once from params. */
export function derived(p: EscapementParams) {
  const pitch = 360 / p.teeth;
  const halfEmbrace = (2.5 * pitch) / 2; // pallets straddle 2.5 teeth
  const pivotDistance = p.wheelRadius / Math.cos(rad(halfEmbrace)); // tangential geometry
  const stoneArm = p.wheelRadius * Math.tan(rad(halfEmbrace)); // pivot to tangent point
  const forkHalf = (p.lockAngle + p.liftLever + p.runToBanking) / 2;
  const liftWheel = pitch / 2 - p.drop;
  return { pitch, halfEmbrace, pivotDistance, stoneArm, forkHalf, liftWheel };
}

export const rad = (deg: number) => (deg * Math.PI) / 180;
export const deg = (r: number) => (r * 180) / Math.PI;
9:- **balance** — the oscillating wheel. Its angle from rest is `balanceAngle` (degrees). *(spike)*
10:- **hairspring** — the spiral spring returning the balance to rest. Its stiffness sets the period together with balance inertia.
11:- **amplitude** — peak balance angle from rest, degrees. Healthy at full wind: roughly 250–300° dial up. *(spike, as `balanceAmplitude`)*
12:- **beat** — one half-swing of the balance, from one extreme to the other. One tick. *(spike)*
15:- **regulator index** — the lever that slides the curb pins along the hairspring, changing its active length and so the rate. Marked F/S or +/−.
16:- **timing screws** — screws on the balance rim; turning them in or out changes balance inertia and so the rate.
17:- **stud** — the fixed outer anchor of the hairspring. Rotating the stud carrier changes where the balance rests relative to the fork: the **beat adjustment**.
18:- **poise** — the balance's mass balance about its axis. A **poise error** (heavy spot) changes rate in vertical positions.
23:- **escape wheel** — the toothed wheel the gear train drives; released one half-tooth per beat. `wheelAngle` is degrees of rotation in the direction of tooth travel. *(spike)*
25:- **pallet fork** (lever) — the pivoted piece carrying two pallet stones and the notch. Its angle from centre is `forkAngle`. *(spike)*
26:- **pallet stone** (pallet) — the jewel that stops and then pushes the escape wheel. **Entry** stone meets each tooth first; **exit** stone last. *(spike)*
30:- **lock** — the phase with the tooth at rest on a locking face. `lockAngle` is the lever rotation needed to unlock. *(spike)*

# Hyperframes Composition Brief: The Watchmaker's Bench

## Objective
Create a short launch-style brag video for The Watchmaker's Bench.

## Output
- Composition directory: `brag-output/composition/`
- Rendered video: `brag-output/brag.mp4`
- Format: landscape — 1920x1080
- Duration: 24.5 seconds

## Source Material
- Project root: the repository root (one level above `brag-output/`)
- Primary files read: `index.html` (markup, CSS tokens), `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GLOSSARY.md`, `src/puzzles/index.ts`, `src/view/movement.ts`, `src/view/timegrapher.ts`, `src/main.ts`, `src/core/**`, `src/verify/states.ts`
- Product name: The Watchmaker's Bench
- Tagline / strongest claim: "Diagnose a live movement and regulate it, reading the timegrapher the way a watchmaker does."
- Key UI or visual moment to recreate: puzzle 1 solved on the three-column bench: sloping trace, Regulator index dragged toward S, trace flat, "solved"
- Copy that must appear verbatim:
  - "The owner says it gains about 40 seconds a day."
  - "The Watchmaker's Bench"
  - "Diagnose a live movement and regulate it." (trimmed tagline)
  - "Puzzle 1 · Runs fast" with its goal text, "Regulator index", "State of wind"
  - "Why it worked" / "The regulator index had been pushed toward F."
  - "Out of beat", "Afternoon slump", "Position error"
  - "Why a watch keeps bad time, and how you fix it." (from the project's own description of itself)
  - "watchmakers-bench.pages.dev"

## Creative Direction
- Tone preset: polished
- Creative direction: quiet drafting-sheet product film; an instrument, a drawing, one adjustment
- Interpretation: few scenes, long holds, soft crossfades, no hype copy. The watch supplies the motion.
- Angle: a watch comes in with a complaint and the video is the repair. The drawing and the instrument are the app's own renderers driven by its own sim, frame by frame, so the video shows the product working rather than a picture of it.
- Hook: dark screen, the trace draws itself sloping, "+41 s/day", the symptom line, ticking.
- Outro / punchline: "Why a watch keeps bad time, and how you fix it." and the URL.
- Avoid:
  - Generic SaaS language
  - Abstract filler visuals
  - Unrelated visual redesign
  - The words "Swiss lever" (project decision: say "lever" until club teeth exist)

- Text: `#1c2733` ink, `#4a5663` secondary

/**
 * The film's script as pure functions of film time. Shared by the offline pose precompute
 * (build/build.mjs) and the browser runtime (film.ts), so both agree on what the watch is
 * doing at every frame. Nothing here touches the DOM.
 */
import { VINTAGE_18000 } from "../../../src/catalog/vintage18000";
import { nominalPeriod } from "../../../src/core/oscillator/period";
import { readWatch, ZERO_SETTINGS } from "../../../src/core/watch";
import { PUZZLES } from "../../../src/puzzles";

export const FPS = 60;
export const DURATION = 24.5;
export const FRAMES = Math.round(FPS * DURATION);

/** Scene boundaries, film seconds (see brag-plan.md). */
export const S2 = 3.82, S3 = 8.19, S4 = 16.38, S5 = 20.75;
/** Scene 3 beats: cursor grabs the regulator, lets go, puzzle reads solved. */
export const GRAB = 8.74, RELEASE = 10.4, SOLVED = 13.11;

/** Music beat grid: vol-12 at 109.96 BPM, a beat on 3.818 s. */
export const BEAT = 0.5456, BEAT0 = 3.818;

export const calibre = VINTAGE_18000;
export const esc = calibre.escapement;
export const T = nominalPeriod(calibre.beatRate);

/** Movement speed that lands one beat of the watch on every second beat of the music. */
export const BEAT_LOCKED_SPEED = (T / 2) / (2 * BEAT);
/** The app's "1/5" stop, used on the bench where the speed strip is visible. */
export const BENCH_SPEED = 0.2;

/** Film-time spans in which the movement drawing is on screen. Poses are precomputed for these. */
export const SEG_A = { from: 3.2, to: 17.0 };
export const SEG_B = { from: 20.1, to: DURATION };

/** Watch seconds elapsed on the movement view at film time t. Continuous within each segment. */
export function movementTime(t: number): number {
  if (t < SEG_B.from) {
    if (t <= S3) return (t - BEAT0) * BEAT_LOCKED_SPEED;
    return (S3 - BEAT0) * BEAT_LOCKED_SPEED + (t - S3) * BENCH_SPEED;
  }
  // Outro: re-locked so a tick lands on 22.91 s, where the URL arrives.
  return (t - (BEAT0 + 31 * BEAT)) * BEAT_LOCKED_SPEED + 40 * T;
}

/** Amplitude of puzzle 1's watch at full wind, dial up (the regulator does not change it). */
export const AMPLITUDE = readWatch(calibre.watch, { ...ZERO_SETTINGS, ...PUZZLES[0].faults }).amplitudeDeg;

/** Balance angle on the movement view, degrees. In beat: it crosses the notch centre at zero. */
export function balanceAngle(t: number): number {
  return AMPLITUDE * Math.sin((2 * Math.PI * movementTime(t)) / T);
}

const clamp01 = (x: number) => Math.max(0, Math.min(1, x));
export const smooth = (x: number) => { const u = clamp01(x); return u * u * (3 - 2 * u); };
export const ramp = (t: number, t0: number, t1: number) => clamp01((t - t0) / (t1 - t0));

/** Regulator index the hand has set, degrees (slider step 0.05). Overshoots a little, then corrects. */
export function regulatorAt(t: number): number {
  let v = 0;
  if (t >= GRAB) {
    const over = -1.35, rest = -1.2, turn = GRAB + 1.15;
    v = t < turn ? over * smooth(ramp(t, GRAB, turn)) : over + (rest - over) * smooth(ramp(t, turn, RELEASE));
  }
  return Math.round(v / 0.05) * 0.05;
}

/**
 * Offline: step the app's real escapement (contact solver and all) along the film's balance
 * trajectory and write one pose per film frame. The stepper is too heavy to run per frame in
 * the browser; its output is a few numbers per frame.
 */
import { initialPose, step, type EscapementPose } from "../../../src/core/escapement/kinematics";
import { FPS, SEG_A, SEG_B, balanceAngle, movementTime, esc } from "./scenario";

const PHASES = ["lock", "unlock", "impulse", "drop"];
const CONTACTS = [null, "entry/locking", "entry/impulse", "exit/locking", "exit/impulse"];

function segment(seg: { from: number; to: number }) {
  const f0 = Math.ceil(seg.from * FPS), f1 = Math.floor(seg.to * FPS);
  // Warm up for two film seconds so the wheel has settled into its rhythm before the first frame.
  const warm = 2 * FPS;
  let t = (f0 - warm) / FPS;
  let pose: EscapementPose = initialPose(esc, balanceAngle(t));
  const rows: (number | string)[][] = [];
  let violations = 0;
  for (let f = f0 - warm + 1; f <= f1; f++) {
    const nt = f / FPS;
    pose = step(esc, pose, balanceAngle(nt), Math.max(1e-6, movementTime(nt) - movementTime(t)));
    t = nt;
    if (f >= f0) {
      const c = pose.contact ? `${pose.contact.stone}/${pose.contact.face}` : null;
      rows.push([+pose.balanceAngle.toFixed(3), +pose.forkAngle.toFixed(4), +pose.wheelAngle.toFixed(4), PHASES.indexOf(pose.phase), CONTACTS.indexOf(c)]);
    }
  }
  violations = pose.violations;
  return { f0, rows, violations };
}

const A = segment(SEG_A), B = segment(SEG_B);
const out = `/* Generated by build/build.mjs from src/precompute.ts. Do not edit. */\nwindow.__POSES = ${JSON.stringify({ phases: PHASES, contacts: CONTACTS, segments: [{ f0: A.f0, rows: A.rows }, { f0: B.f0, rows: B.rows }] })};\n`;
process.stdout.write(out);
process.stderr.write(`poses: A ${A.rows.length} frames (violations ${A.violations}), B ${B.rows.length} frames (violations ${B.violations})\n`);

import type { EscapementPose, Phase } from "../../../src/core/escapement/kinematics";
import { FPS, DURATION, FRAMES, S2, S3, S4, S5, GRAB, RELEASE, SOLVED, BEAT, BEAT0, T, calibre, esc, BENCH_SPEED, movementTime, regulatorAt, smooth, ramp } from "./scenario";

export { FPS, DURATION, FRAMES, S2, S3, S4, S5, GRAB, RELEASE, SOLVED, BEAT, BEAT0 };

const TRACE_BEATS = 300;
/** What the app's own label says (main.ts SIM_SPEEDUP). The film's edit runs the instrument faster. */
const SIM_SPEEDUP = 10;

// ---------- a watch on the instrument, as a function of film frame ----------
interface SimDef {
  spec: WatchSpec;
  faults: Partial<WatchSettings>;
  user: (t: number) => WatchSettings;
  /** Instrument seconds elapsed at film time t (monotonic). */
  simTime: (t: number) => number;
  /** Ticks already on the screen at frame 0, in instrument seconds. */
  prefill: number;
  band?: Puzzle["band"];
  holdSeconds?: number;
}
interface SimState { win: TickWindow; held: number; solved: boolean }

class Sim {
  private states: SimState[] = [];
  constructor(private def: SimDef) {}
  effective(t: number): WatchSettings {
    const user = this.def.user(t), f = this.def.faults;
    // Same sum as main.ts effective(): hidden faults plus the user's adjustments.
    return {
      ...user,
      regulatorIndex: user.regulatorIndex + (f.regulatorIndex ?? 0),
      beatOffsetDeg: user.beatOffsetDeg + (f.beatOffsetDeg ?? 0),
      unbalance: user.unbalance + (f.unbalance ?? 0),
      heavySpotDeg: f.heavySpotDeg ?? user.heavySpotDeg,
    };
  }
  reading(t: number): WatchReading { return readWatch(this.def.spec, this.effective(t)); }
  state(frame: number): SimState {
    const d = this.def;
    while (this.states.length <= frame) {
      const i = this.states.length, t = i / FPS, r = this.reading(t);
      if (i === 0) {
        this.states.push({ win: advanceTicks(emptyWindow(), r, d.simTime(0), TRACE_BEATS), held: 0, solved: false });
        continue;
      }
      const prev = this.states[i - 1];
      const win = advanceTicks(prev.win, r, d.simTime(t), TRACE_BEATS);
      let held = prev.held, solved = prev.solved;
      if (d.band && !solved) {
        const ds = d.simTime(t) - d.simTime((i - 1) / FPS);
        held = d.band(r, analyze(win.ticks, T, calibre.liftAngle)) ? held + ds : 0;
        if (held >= (d.holdSeconds ?? Infinity)) solved = true;
      }
      this.states.push({ win, held, solved });
    }
    return this.states[frame];
  }
  tg(frame: number): Reading | null { return analyze(this.state(frame).win.ticks, T, calibre.liftAngle); }
  html(frame: number): string {
    const r = this.reading(frame / FPS);
    return renderTimegrapher({ reading: this.tg(frame), nominalPeriod: T, liftAngle: calibre.liftAngle, running: r.running, knocking: r.knocking, spanSeconds: (TRACE_BEATS * T) / 2, speedup: SIM_SPEEDUP });
  }
}

const clamp = (x: number, lo: number, hi: number) => Math.max(lo, Math.min(hi, x));

// Puzzle 1 on the main instrument. The trace grows through scene 1, waits through scene 2,
// and runs again on the bench. After the hand lets go, the clock runs at whatever speed puts
// the app's real completion rule (60 instrument seconds in band) on the "solved" cue.
const P1 = PUZZLES[0];
const mainUser = (t: number): WatchSettings => ({ ...ZERO_SETTINGS, regulatorIndex: regulatorAt(t) });
let afterRelease = 30;
const mainSimTime = (t: number) =>
  18 * clamp(t - 0.25, 0, S2 - 0.25) + 20 * clamp(t - (S3 - 0.5), 0, RELEASE - (S3 - 0.5)) + afterRelease * Math.max(0, t - RELEASE);
const mainDef: SimDef = { spec: calibre.watch, faults: P1.faults, user: mainUser, simTime: mainSimTime, prefill: 0, band: P1.band, holdSeconds: P1.holdSeconds };
{
  // Instrument seconds from release to solved do not depend on the clock speed, so measure them once.
  const probe = new Sim(mainDef);
  const rel = Math.round(RELEASE * FPS);
  let { win, held } = probe.state(rel);
  const r = probe.reading(RELEASE + 1), ds = 0.25;
  let s = mainSimTime(rel / FPS), elapsed = 0;
  while (held < P1.holdSeconds && elapsed < 600) {
    s += ds; elapsed += ds;
    win = advanceTicks(win, r, s, TRACE_BEATS);
    held = P1.band(r, analyze(win.ticks, T, calibre.liftAngle)) ? held + ds : 0;
  }
  afterRelease = elapsed / (SOLVED - RELEASE);
}
const main = new Sim(mainDef);

// Scene 4: the other three puzzles, each running on its own small instrument.
const miniClock = (speed: number) => (t: number) => 60 + speed * Math.max(0, t - S4);
const beatAt = (t: number) => Math.round((-6 * smooth(ramp(t, 18.0, 18.7))) / 0.1) * 0.1;
const windAt = (t: number) => Math.round((30 * smooth(ramp(t, 18.3, 20.3))) / 0.5) * 0.5;
const positionAt = (t: number): WatchSettings["position"] => (t < 18.9 ? "CU" : "CD");
const minis: { sim: Sim; value: (t: number) => string }[] = [
  {
    sim: new Sim({ spec: calibre.watch, faults: PUZZLES[1].faults, user: (t) => ({ ...ZERO_SETTINGS, beatOffsetDeg: beatAt(t) }), simTime: miniClock(30), prefill: 60 }),
    value: (t) => `${beatAt(t).toFixed(1)}°`,
  },
  {
    sim: new Sim({ spec: PUZZLES[2].specOverride!(calibre.watch), faults: PUZZLES[2].faults, user: (t) => ({ ...ZERO_SETTINGS, hoursSinceWind: windAt(t) }), simTime: miniClock(30), prefill: 60 }),
    value: (t) => `${windAt(t).toFixed(0)} h since wound`,
  },
  {
    sim: new Sim({ spec: calibre.watch, faults: PUZZLES[3].faults, user: (t) => ({ ...ZERO_SETTINGS, position: positionAt(t) }), simTime: miniClock(40), prefill: 60 }),
    value: (t) => POSITIONS.find((p) => p.id === positionAt(t))!.label,
  },
];

// ---------- the movement drawing ----------
interface PoseData { phases: Phase[]; contacts: (string | null)[]; segments: { f0: number; rows: number[][] }[] }
function poseAt(frame: number): EscapementPose {
  const data = (window as any).__POSES as PoseData;
  const seg = frame >= data.segments[1].f0 ? data.segments[1] : data.segments[0];
  const row = seg.rows[clamp(frame - seg.f0, 0, seg.rows.length - 1)];
  const c = data.contacts[row[4]];
  const [stone, face] = c ? c.split("/") : [];
  return { balanceAngle: row[0], forkAngle: row[1], wheelAngle: row[2], phase: data.phases[row[3]], contact: c ? ({ stone, face } as any) : null, violations: 0, maxNudge: 0 };
}
function movementHtml(frame: number, eff: WatchSettings, amplitudeDeg: number, hot: Highlight): string {
  const pose = poseAt(frame);
  const adj = adjustmentShapes(esc, { ...eff, balanceAngle: pose.balanceAngle, amplitudeDeg, revealHeavySpot: false });
  return renderMovement(esc, pose, movementTime(frame / FPS) * 1000, adj, hot);
}

// ---------- the job card (same markup as main.ts puzzleHtml) ----------
function puzzleHtml(puzzle: Puzzle, heldSeconds: number, solved: boolean): string {
  const idx = PUZZLES.indexOf(puzzle);
  const explanation = puzzle.explanation.replace(/^(.*?\.)\s/, "<mark>$1</mark> ");
  return `<h2>Puzzle ${idx + 1} · ${puzzle.title}</h2>
    <p class="symptom">${puzzle.symptom}</p>
    <p class="goal"><strong>Goal:</strong> ${puzzle.goal}</p>
    <div class="hold"><div class="bar" style="width:${Math.min(100, (100 * heldSeconds) / puzzle.holdSeconds).toFixed(1)}%"></div><span>${solved ? "solved" : `${heldSeconds.toFixed(0)} / ${puzzle.holdSeconds} s in band`}</span></div>
    ${solved ? `<details open><summary>Why it worked</summary><p>${explanation}</p></details>` : ""}`;
}

// ---------- mounting ----------
export function mount(): (frame: number) => void {
  const $ = <E extends HTMLElement>(id: string) => document.getElementById(id) as E;
  const root = $("root");
  const last = new Map<Element, string>();
  const put = (el: Element, html: string) => { if (last.get(el) !== html) { last.set(el, html); el.innerHTML = html; } };
  const text = (el: Element, s: string) => { if (last.get(el) !== s) { last.set(el, s); el.textContent = s; } };

  // Static bench furniture, filled the way main.ts fills it.
  $("calibre-name").textContent = calibre.name;
  $<HTMLSelectElement>("puzzle-select").innerHTML = `<option>Puzzle 1: ${P1.title}</option>`;
  mountSpeedControl($("tempo"), $<HTMLSelectElement>("speed"), $("pause"));
  const speedSlider = $<HTMLInputElement>("speed-slider");
  speedSlider.value = String(SPEED_STOPS.findIndex((s) => s.value === BENCH_SPEED));
  speedSlider.dispatchEvent(new Event("input"));
  $("wind-value").textContent = "0 h since wound";

  // Scene 2 drafting labels: an overlay sharing the movement's viewBox, so label anchors are scene coordinates.
  const first = movementHtml(Math.round(S2 * FPS), main.effective(S2), main.reading(S2).amplitudeDeg, null);
  const viewBox = /viewBox="([^"]+)"/.exec(first)![1];
  const { forkPivot, balanceCentre } = fixedPoints(esc);
  const [vx, , vw] = viewBox.split(" ").map(Number);
  const right = vx + vw + 14;
  const label = (id: string, at: { x: number; y: number }, y: number, name: string) =>
    `<g id="${id}" class="callout"><circle cx="${at.x}" cy="${-at.y}" r="2.2"/><polyline points="${at.x},${-at.y} ${right - 22},${-y} ${right},${-y}"/><text x="${right + 5}" y="${-y + 4.2}">${name}</text></g>`;
  $("mv-labels").innerHTML = `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="${viewBox}">${
    label("lab-wheel", { x: esc.wheelRadius * 0.74, y: -esc.wheelRadius * 0.3 }, -52, "escape wheel") +
    label("lab-fork", { x: 9, y: forkPivot.y + 34 }, forkPivot.y + 22, "pallet fork") +
    label("lab-balance", { x: esc.balanceRadius * 0.82, y: balanceCentre.y + esc.balanceRadius * 0.57 }, balanceCentre.y + 62, "balance")
  }</svg>`;

  const tgHero = $("tg-hero"), mvHero = $("mv-hero"), mvOutro = $("mv-outro");
  const benchTg = $("timegrapher"), benchMv = $("movement"), puzzleEl = $("puzzle");
  const regulator = $<HTMLInputElement>("regulator"), regulatorValue = $("regulator-value"), trueRate = $("readout-rate");
  const cursor = $("cursor");
  const glows = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(".tg-glow"));
  const miniEls = [1, 2, 3].map((n) => ({ tg: document.querySelector(`#mini-${n} .tg-case`)!, value: document.querySelector(`#mini-${n} .value`)! }));
  const rms = ((window as any).__RMS as number[]) ?? [];

  /** Centre of the regulator slider's thumb, in stage pixels. */
  const thumb = (value: number) => {
    const rr = root.getBoundingClientRect(), k = rr.width / 1920, r = regulator.getBoundingClientRect();
    const tw = 10 * (r.width / regulator.offsetWidth);
    const frac = (value - Number(regulator.min)) / (Number(regulator.max) - Number(regulator.min));
    return { x: (r.left + tw / 2 + frac * (r.width - tw) - rr.left) / k, y: (r.top + r.height / 2 - rr.top) / k };
  };

  return (f: number) => {
    const frame = clamp(Math.round(f), 0, FRAMES), t = frame / FPS;

    // Main instrument: scene 1 hero and the bench.
    if (t < S2 + 0.3) put(tgHero, main.html(frame));
    if (t > S3 - 0.6 && t < S4 + 0.3) {
      const st = main.state(frame), eff = main.effective(t), r = main.reading(t), v = regulatorAt(t);
      put(benchTg, main.html(frame));
      put(puzzleEl, puzzleHtml(P1, st.held, st.solved));
      const dragging = t >= GRAB && t < RELEASE + 0.15;
      put(benchMv, movementHtml(frame, eff, r.amplitudeDeg, dragging ? "regulator" : null));
      regulator.value = String(v);
      // Same formats as main.ts bindRange("regulator") and drawControls().
      text(regulatorValue, `${v >= 0 ? "+" : "−"}${Math.abs(v).toFixed(2)}° ${v > 0 ? "(toward F)" : v < 0 ? "(toward S)" : ""}`);
      text(trueRate, `${r.rateSecondsPerDay >= 0 ? "+" : "−"}${Math.abs(r.rateSecondsPerDay).toFixed(1)} s/day true rate`);

      // The hand: glide in, hold the thumb through the drag, let go and leave.
      const at = thumb(v), away = { x: at.x + 150, y: at.y + 170 };
      const inU = smooth(ramp(t, S3 + 0.05, GRAB - 0.04)), outU = smooth(ramp(t, RELEASE + 0.1, RELEASE + 1.0));
      const x = t < GRAB ? away.x + (at.x - away.x) * inU : at.x + (away.x - at.x) * outU;
      const y = t < GRAB ? away.y + (at.y - away.y) * inU : at.y + (away.y - at.y) * outU;
      cursor.style.transform = `translate(${x.toFixed(1)}px, ${(y + 3).toFixed(1)}px) scale(${dragging ? 0.88 : 1})`;
      cursor.style.opacity = (t < GRAB ? ramp(t, S3 + 0.05, S3 + 0.3) : 1 - ramp(t, RELEASE + 0.6, RELEASE + 1.0)).toFixed(3);
    }

    // Movement as hero (scene 2) and in the outro (free play: healthy watch, nothing touched).
    if (t > S2 - 0.6 && t < S3 + 0.3) put(mvHero, movementHtml(frame, main.effective(t), main.reading(t).amplitudeDeg, null));
    if (t > S5 - 0.6) put(mvOutro, movementHtml(frame, { ...ZERO_SETTINGS }, readWatch(calibre.watch, ZERO_SETTINGS).amplitudeDeg, null));

    // Scene 4 instruments.
    if (t > S4 - 0.6 && t < S5 + 0.3) minis.forEach((m, i) => { put(miniEls[i].tg, m.sim.html(frame)); text(miniEls[i].value, m.value(t)); });

    // Phosphor glow breathes with the music's loudness.
    const level = rms[Math.min(frame, rms.length - 1)] ?? 0;
    for (const g of glows) g.style.opacity = (0.3 + 0.7 * level).toFixed(3);
  };
}

/** Numbers the build prints so the timeline cues can be checked against the sim. */
export function report() {
  let solvedAt = -1;
  for (let f = 0; f <= FRAMES && solvedAt < 0; f++) if (main.state(f).solved) solvedAt = f / FPS;
  const at = (t: number) => { const f = Math.round(t * FPS), g = main.tg(f); return g ? `${g.rateSecondsPerDay.toFixed(1)} s/day, ${g.amplitudeDeg.toFixed(0)}°, ${g.beatErrorMs.toFixed(2)} ms` : "no reading"; };
  const mini = (i: number, t: number) => { const g = minis[i].sim.tg(Math.round(t * FPS)); return g ? `${g.rateSecondsPerDay.toFixed(1)} s/day, ${g.amplitudeDeg.toFixed(0)}°, ${g.beatErrorMs.toFixed(2)} ms` : "no reading"; };
  return {
    afterReleaseSpeed: afterRelease, solvedAt,
    main: { "1.0": at(1), "3.5": at(3.5), "8.7": at(8.7), "10.4": at(10.4), "12.0": at(12), "13.2": at(13.2), "16.0": at(16) },
    minis: [0, 1, 2].map((i) => ({ "17.0": mini(i, 17), "18.8": mini(i, 18.8), "20.5": mini(i, 20.5) })),
  };
}

/**
 * Builds the three generated scripts the composition loads:
 *   bench.js  the app's sim core and renderers plus the film runtime (src/film.ts), as one IIFE
 *   poses.js  one escapement pose per film frame (src/precompute.ts run under Node)
 *   rms.js    per-frame loudness of the music bed, for the phosphor glow
 * Run from the repository root after `npm ci`:  node brag-output/composition/build/build.mjs
 * Needs ffmpeg on PATH for rms.js.
 */
import { build } from "esbuild";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { writeFileSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const comp = join(here, "..");
const FPS = 60; // keep in step with src/scenario.ts

await build({ entryPoints: [join(comp, "src/film.ts")], bundle: true, format: "iife", globalName: "Bench", target: "es2020", outfile: join(comp, "bench.js"), banner: { js: "/* Generated by build/build.mjs from src/film.ts and the app's src/. Do not edit. */" } });

const tmp = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "brag-build-"));
try {
  await build({ entryPoints: [join(comp, "src/precompute.ts")], bundle: true, format: "cjs", platform: "node", outfile: join(tmp, "precompute.cjs") });
  writeFileSync(join(comp, "poses.js"), execFileSync("node", [join(tmp, "precompute.cjs")], { maxBuffer: 1 << 26, stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "inherit"] }));

  // The runtime's own numbers, so the timeline cues can be checked against the sim.
  await build({ entryPoints: [join(comp, "src/film.ts")], bundle: true, format: "cjs", platform: "node", outfile: join(tmp, "film.cjs") });
  const film = (await import(join(tmp, "film.cjs"))).default;
  console.log(JSON.stringify(film.report(), null, 1));
} finally {
  rmSync(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
}

const rate = 6000, per = rate / FPS;
const pcm = execFileSync("ffmpeg", ["-v", "error", "-i", join(comp, "assets/music/vol-12-bed.mp3"), "-ac", "1", "-ar", String(rate), "-f", "f32le", "-"], { maxBuffer: 1 << 28 });
const samples = new Float32Array(pcm.buffer, pcm.byteOffset, Math.floor(pcm.byteLength / 4));
const raw = [];
for (let i = 0; i + per <= samples.length; i += per) {
  let sum = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < per; j++) sum += samples[i + j] ** 2;
  raw.push(Math.sqrt(sum / per));
}
const ref = [...raw].sort((a, b) => a - b)[Math.floor(raw.length * 0.95)] || 1;
const smoothed = raw.map((_, i) => {
  let sum = 0, n = 0;
  for (let j = Math.max(0, i - 5); j <= Math.min(raw.length - 1, i + 5); j++) { sum += raw[j]; n++; }
  return +Math.min(1, sum / n / ref).toFixed(3);
});
writeFileSync(join(comp, "rms.js"), `/* Generated by build/build.mjs: music loudness per film frame (0..1). Do not edit. */\nwindow.__RMS = ${JSON.stringify(smoothed)};\n`);
console.log(`rms: ${smoothed.length} frames`);
